title: Pump and Dump: How Hype Can Trap Beginners in Small Coins
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. A pump and dump is when hype pushes a small asset up so insiders can sell to latecomers. Sources: SEC Investor.gov, Investopedia. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: WHY DID IT SPIKE?
scenes.narration: A tiny coin jumps fifty percent in an hour, and everyone is posting about it. Is it real, or a pump and dump?

scenes.head: THE PUMP
scenes.sub: HYPE PUSHES A SMALL COIN UP
scenes.narration: In a pump, a group hypes a small, thinly traded coin online. New buyers rush in, and the price jumps fast.

scenes.head: THE DUMP
scenes.narration: In the dump, the people who bought early sell into that demand. The hype stops, and late buyers are left holding the loss.

scenes.head: WHY SMALL COINS?
scenes.narration: Small coins have low trading volume, so a little money can move the price a lot. That makes them a common target.

scenes.head: WARNING SIGNS
scenes.narration: Regulators warn about guaranteed returns, pressure to act right now, and secret tips from strangers in online groups.

scenes.head: SMARTER HABITS
scenes.narration: Before reacting to hype, check for real news, look at trading volume, and remember that a fast spike can reverse just as fast.
